newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Renault says no basis for Belgian action.
newsitem.headline: Renault says no basis for Belgian action.

text.p: GENEVA, March 4 (Reter) - French carmaker Renault SA does not believe Belgian authorities have any legal grounds to take action against its planned closure of the Vilvoorde plant, a senior company executive said on Tuesday.
"My feeling is that we have completely respected all the procedures," said Michel de Virville, senior vice-president in charge of personnel and external relations.
He told reporters at the Geneva Car Show that the closure did not reflect the quality of work at the plant but was essential for the group's industrial strategy.

Renault says the closure, with the loss of 3,100 jobs and a charge of 2.4 billion French francs ($416.4 million) on its 1996 results, will streamline production so that fewer models are made in more than one plant.
The combinations of model per plant will be reduced to eight at the end of 1997 from 12 currently.
In 1998, when the Twingo is no longer made in the Spanish plant at Valladolid, that figure will drop to seven combinations per plant.
"The announcement puts us in a competitive situation to the year 2000," de Virville said.
Renault is expected later this month to announce an operating loss of more than two billion francs as well as the Belgian restructuring charge and possibly other job-cutting costs.
